record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, does there exist a global smooth solution for arbitrary smooth data? More broadly, what are the asymptotic behaviors of Navier-Stokes solutions as time goes to infinity or as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, do inertial manifolds exist for the two- and three-dimensional equations, is Prandtl boundary-layer theory valid for viscous incompressible flow near boundaries, and what asymptotic forms arise when the limiting Euler solution is singular?

evidence.quote: Regularity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Although there is no evidence either numerically or physically to support the breaking down of smooth solutions to the 3-D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, yet the global (in time) existence of smooth to the 3-D incompressible Navier-Stokes system is one of the most challenging mathematical problems to be solved.

Other important open problems include: asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations either as time approaches infinitely or as Reynold number goes to infinity; do inertial manifolds exist for 2-D or 3-D Navier-Stokes equations [50]? Is Prandtl's boundary layer theory valid for the viscous incompressible fluids in the presence of boundary [43, 46]? What are the asymptotic forms of the solutions to the Navier-Stokes system as the Reynold number goes to infinity in the case of corresponding Euler solutions are singular?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (or on the torus $\mathbb{T}^3$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu\Delta u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with viscosity $\nu>0$, where $u:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}^3$ is the velocity field and $p$ is the pressure. Address the following questions.

(a) Global regularity. Given an arbitrary divergence-free initial datum $u_0\in C^\infty$ (with suitable decay at infinity, or periodic), does there exist a smooth solution $u\in C^\infty([0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^3)$ to the above system with $u(0,\cdot)=u_0$? Equivalently, can smooth finite-energy data develop a singularity in finite time?

(b) Long-time asymptotics. Describe the asymptotic behavior of Leray–Hopf weak solutions (or smooth solutions when they exist) as $t\to\infty$, both in two and three dimensions.

(c) High Reynolds number asymptotics. Describe the asymptotic behavior of solutions as the Reynolds number $Re = 1/\nu \to \infty$, in particular when the formal limit (Euler) solution develops singularities.

(d) Inertial manifolds. Do the two-dimensional and/or three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a finite-dimensional inertial manifold, i.e. a finite-dimensional smooth invariant manifold in phase space which is exponentially attracting and contains the global attractor?

(e) Prandtl boundary layer theory. In a domain with boundary and no-slip boundary condition, as $\nu\to 0$, is Prandtl's boundary-layer ansatz mathematically justified for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, i.e. can the vanishing viscosity limit be rigorously described by an outer Euler flow matched to an inner Prandtl boundary-layer profile?
artifact.status_search_result: The global regularity question for the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations is one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains open. The related questions on long-time and high-Reynolds-number asymptotics, existence of inertial manifolds for 2D and 3D Navier-Stokes (3D inertial manifold existence is widely open; even in 2D existence of a classical inertial manifold remains unresolved), and the rigorous validity of Prandtl boundary-layer theory for incompressible flows are all recognized as outstanding open problems in mathematical fluid dynamics as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness — Clay Mathematics Institute
status_evidence.snippet: Prove or give a counter-example of the following statement: In three space dimensions and time, given an initial velocity field, there exists a vector velocity and a scalar pressure field, which are both smooth and globally defined...
status_evidence.claim: The 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes global regularity problem is an unsolved Millennium Prize Problem.

status_evidence.title: Inertial manifolds for the Navier-Stokes equations (survey literature)
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of an inertial manifold for the 2D Navier–Stokes equations is a long-standing open problem; for the 3D equations the question is even more out of reach.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of inertial manifolds for 2D/3D Navier-Stokes remains open.

status_evidence.title: Recent progress on the mathematical theory of Prandtl equations
status_evidence.snippet: The rigorous justification of Prandtl's boundary layer theory in the vanishing viscosity limit for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary condition remains a major open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Validity of Prandtl boundary-layer theory is open in general.
